text:
alex: Heads up — support ticket #4567. Several customers reporting p99 latency spikes starting this morning after the 03/01 infra roll. Tickets show timeouts and 504s. Dashboard p99 for /v1/generate jumped to ~1.8s (was ~600ms). :eyes:

maria: saw it too. Pager fired for p99 alert at 07:12. The raw histogram panel and the p99 line on the overview disagree — histogram seems consistent with previous numbers.

zhang: FYI I touched the metrics exporter buckets in the 03/01 deploy to reduce cardinality. I moved us from exponential buckets to fixed log-spaced buckets for token_latency_hist. Could be a bucketization artifact.

josh: can you share the queries you used? I ran two quick PromQL checks:
```
# dashboard query (rolled-up quantile)
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(token_latency_hist_bucket[5m])) by (le))

# raw histogram-based approximate (from distribution)
quantile_over_time(0.99, token_latency_seconds_bucket[5m])  # (example)
```
The dashboard's saved query is the first one. The raw panel uses a t-digest aggregation via our analytics cluster. Results differ: dashboard 1.8s, t-digest 0.65s.

sre-bot: Alert: p99_latency_high fired for /v1/generate at 1795001125 (sev3).

kd: This smells like a histogram bucket boundary mismatch. histogram_quantile assumes the buckets are continuous and monotonic. If you coarsened or changed boundaries, the quantile calc can overshoot. Also note that exponential->log spacing shifts mass in the upper tail which disproportionately affects p99.

alex: do we have traces for any failing requests? Soph, any example from support?

sophia: attaching a repro trace from customer A (trace id: 0000-aaa-1795). Request shows multiple retries; server side tail latency is still ~600ms. Client saw timeouts because their retry logic hits client-side timeout at 1s. Link: https://dash.redwood.internal/traces/0000-aaa-1795 :link: 

maria: confirmed — traces don't show 1.8s server processing. So dashboard p99 looks wrong, probably calculation issue.

zhang: quick check of exporter commit — I added a transformation that aggregates per-model latency into wider buckets before export to reduce series. That was intended but I didn't update the Grafana panels. My bad.

josh: suggested mitigations: (1) revert bucket transform on exporter (hotfix), (2) change dashboard to use t-digest quantiles from analytics cluster, or (3) change alerts to use the raw percentile from traces/t-digest as temporary source of truth.

alex: we need an emergency mitigation to stop noisy alerts and stop telling support it's a system outage. Which is fastest?

kd: fastest is to flip the alert to a different query that uses the t-digest-derived metric we already ingest into metrics-analytics. I'll patch the alert rule to use `analytics_quantile_approx(token_latency, 0.99)` alias.

maria: I'll create a short-lived dashboard panel that points at the analytics quantile and promote it to the overview. Also turning off the p99 metric email alert until we decide. :no_entry_sign:

deploy-bot: Canary deploy of metrics-exporter rollback started at 1795001240 for tag v3.2.1 -> v3.1.9.

zhang: deploying rollback, monitoring exporter logs now. If rollback completes, bucket boundaries will revert.

sre-bot: Canary deploy complete at 1795001275. No errors in canary.

maria: after the rollback the dashboard p99 dropped to 0.68s within two minutes. I updated the alert rule to point to analytics quantile and silenced the old rule.

alex: nice. Next steps:
- zhang open PR to add a compatibility flag when changing buckets and document dash changes
- kd validate histogram_quantile assumptions in our dashboards and add unit tests
- josh and soph create a KB article for support explaining the discrepancy and how we triage
- maria keep the alert using analytics_quantile for 48h and then we'll evaluate

zhang: opening PR now with notes and a README entry. Sorry everyone.

josh: logged follow-up ticket RW-9123 to migrate critical dashboards to t-digest-derived quantiles and add regression tests.

alex: great. Closing the immediate firefight — thanks for quick responses. We'll follow up in RW-9123 and keep customers updated. :thumbsup:

sre-bot: Incident resolved at 1795001388. Alerts suppressed until 1795001600 for cleanup window.

maria: filing postmortem draft in #postmortems, will ping for review.

sophia: will update support replies with the rollback note and ETA for a permanent fix.

alex: triage complete. Good job team.
